name: feigenbaum-fixed-point-collocation
authority: Research 0129 section 3; this contract authorizes one bounded run and nothing else
question: Can the Feigenbaum constants be obtained by solving the Feigenbaum-Cvitanovic fixed point of the period-doubling operator directly, so that the digits no longer come from an accelerated cascade, and how many published digits does a declared truncation reproduce?
level: External high-precision numerical calibration of a functional equation by truncated-series collocation and Newton iteration; no verified error bounds yet, no stable semantic operation, no native admission
domain: Even functions g(x) = G(x^2) with G(0) = 1, solving G = T[G] where T[G](y) = A G((G(y/A^2))^2) and A = 1/G(1); this is g(x) = -alpha g(g(x/alpha)) with alpha = -1/g(1) = 2.5029... The linearised operator, restricted to the normalised subspace g(0) = 1, has delta = 4.6692... as its dominant eigenvalue. Decimal arithmetic at 70 significant digits; no binary floating point is used for any reported value.

objects.published_source: OEIS A006890, A006891 and A306963, fetched 2026-09-13; b-file digests recorded in experiments/feigenbaum_period_doubling/contract.json

quantifiers: Every truncation degree in the declared list
Every Newton iteration and every finite-difference column of the Jacobian at every degree
Every reported decimal of delta, alpha and g(1) against the recorded published prefixes
acceptance: The Newton iteration converges at every declared degree, and the achieved algebraic residual of the fixed-point equation is reported
The a posteriori truncation residual, the largest coefficient of the fixed-point equation beyond the truncation degree, decreases with the degree and is reported per degree
The number of agreeing leading characters with the published delta and alpha grows with the degree, and at the largest declared degree reaches at least twenty-five characters for both
The normalisation is checked internally: g(1) equals -1/alpha, and the reported 1/alpha is compared with the recorded published reciprocal

The dominant eigenvalue is taken from the linearisation restricted to the normalised subspace; the unrestricted linearisation is computed as a control and its different dominant eigenvalue is reported, so that the spurious direction is visible rather than silently excluded
No extrapolation or acceleration of any kind is applied to the reported digits
protected: The earlier cascade contract and evidence (experiments/feigenbaum_period_doubling) are frozen and are not rewritten; this round may cite them
The published digits are a comparison target with their source and fetch date recorded; their bytes are not retained here
No verified error bound is claimed: the truncation residual is a numerical indicator, not a proved enclosure
Nothing is claimed about whether either constant is algebraic or irrational
No metric, Arakelov, Monge-Ampere, mirror or Calabi-Yau content is introduced
No native Rust witness, library admission or Seal follows from this calibration
residual: This solves one functional equation numerically at a declared truncation and reports how many published digits it reproduces without acceleration. It is not a rigorous computation: a proved enclosure would need interval or ball arithmetic and a Newton-Kantorovich type bound, which is the next step and is not done here. The comparison target is one published source, whose bytes are not retained. Nothing is claimed about the algebraic nature of the constants, about other universality classes, or about the operator's full spectrum beyond the dominant eigenvalue that is reported.
